question: Should OpenClaw accept the RFC's grouped core update executor with compensating partial-state semantics for non-transactional package and Gateway mutations?
rationale: Code review cannot decide whether one consent should span these trust boundaries or whether retained external artifacts are an acceptable permanent lifecycle contract.

options.title: Approve after full-stack proof
options.body: Accept the design only after prerequisite PRs and the RFC are approved and live package, cron, partial-failure, retry, status, and doctor evidence is attached.

options.title: Narrow the mutation scope
options.body: Limit the initial executor to reversible agent, workspace, and validated config owners while deferring package and Gateway mutations to separately consented operations.

options.title: Keep the stack experimental
options.body: Leave this draft unmerged until maintainers settle the broader Claws product and ownership model.

recommendation.title: Approve after full-stack proof
recommendation.body: Accept the design only after prerequisite PRs and the RFC are approved and live package, cron, partial-failure, retry, status, and doctor evidence is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core CLI product direction, plugin installation, cron lifecycle, and compatibility boundaries associated with this person's recent adjacent work.
